evals.prompt: I need to fix a bug in step 3 of my tutorial's demo repo. I'll just move the 'step-3' tag to the new commit.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to move a tag the published piece links to, and instead publish a new tag (e.g. step-3.1) and update the link in the piece, changing piece and repo together.
expectations: Refuses to move a published tag
Publishes a new tag or branch
Updates the piece's link to the new tag

evals.prompt: I committed my Stripe secret key to the demo repo last month. I'll just delete the file in a new commit.
evals.expected_output: Should say deleting the file leaves the key in history: revoke the key at Stripe first, then remove it from history, add .env.example with no values and .env to .gitignore.
expectations: Revokes the key at the issuer first
Explains a new commit leaves it in history

evals.prompt: Set up the companion repo for my React tutorial — the 2026-12-react-forms topic. Readers kept saying it breaks.
evals.expected_output: Should pin the runtime in .nvmrc or similar, commit the lockfile, give only the piece's commands, add a smoke check, run it in CI on push and on a schedule with dependency updates, add a licence file, a 'Tested with' line, and link the piece to an exact tag or commit. Should read the topic's brief.md, the profile and the repo (git remote, version files, lockfile) before asking, ask only what they leave open, and record the repo and its tag in the brief's Demo project row — the repo itself stays out of the publication's folder.
expectations: Pins the runtime in a version file and commits the lockfile
Adds a smoke check run in CI on a schedule
Adds a licence file and a 'Tested with' line
Links the piece to an exact tag or commit
Reads brief.md and the repo before asking, and records the repo and tag in the brief's Demo project row

evals.prompt: Write the README for my tutorial's demo repo.
evals.expected_output: Should resolve the owner first: for the owner's own repo, take author name, publication URL and audience from the publication's profile.md (the folder AGENTS.md or the user's personal agent instructions name, else the project's publications/; in a chat app, the project's files; else ask) and the GitHub handle from the git remote; a third party's repo uses their details. The writing guide's defaults override the README template's.
expectations: Determines whether the repo is the owner's or a third party's
Reads profile.md for author and links
Uses the git remote for the handle
Lets the writing guide override README defaults
